forward_pass.problem: How should one define practical cryptographic security when brute force is finite but enormous?
forward_pass.model: finite key of r bits; adversary knows the method but not the key; ciphertext leaks information about the key; direct exhaustive procedure considers 2^r keys
forward_pass.observation: simple or weakly interacting cipher structures may admit shortcuts whose computation grows only as a low-degree polynomial in r
forward_pass.conjectural_step: sufficiently complex interaction among key-controlled instructions may cause mean key-recovery computation to grow exponentially with key length
forward_pass.consequence_envisioned: computationally unbreakable practical ciphers despite theoretical finite breakability

tranception.reverse_question: Given an interacting finite-key system that appears exponentially hard, what exact invariant/quotient/coordinate change would collapse the interaction without losing key distinguishability?
tranception.janus_translation: Given an OPEN CNF residual, search for a polynomially discoverable exact representation in which the apparent interaction product is not materialized.
